result.title: Update Slope Is Bounded by Prior Calibration: A Structural Bound and Its Contingent Empirical Signature
result.comment: Accepted at the 2026 IEEE International Conference on Tools with Artificial Intelligence (ICTAI 2026). 5 pages
result.summary: Evaluations of LLM forecasters increasingly measure how forecasts improve as richer evidence is supplied. We identify two confounds in this update-slope metric. First, outcome-aware evidence construction substantially inflates measured responsiveness: on the same models and questions, slopes are roughly four times larger than with resolution-blinded evidence ladders. Second, update slope is a change score with a prior-dependent structural ceiling, so raw comparisons can reflect differences in starting calibration rather than updating behavior. The ceiling defines only a feasible region; whether slope and prior calibration are empirically coupled depends on headroom utilization and varies across our Manifold, ForecastBench, and ACLED pools. Despite this variability, conditioning on prior calibration roughly triples the association between intermediate updating and final Brier score under both blinded and outcome-aware construction. Question identity also explains substantially more variance than model identity across the evaluated pools. We recommend building evidence ladders blind to outcomes, conditioning on prior calibration, and reporting headroom-normalized measures alongside raw slopes.

AI.brief_summary: 论文诊断 LLM 预测器「更新斜率」指标的两处混淆：结果可知的证据构造会把响应度放大约四倍，且斜率存在依赖先验校准的结构上限；因此建议使用结果盲化的证据阶梯、以先验校准为条件，并同时报告 headroom 归一化指标。
AI.relevance_reason: 该文对「证据增多带来多少更新」的度量批判，可能可供核查于 LOOK/视觉证据注入的收益评估：收益需按先验能力 headroom 归一化并避免结果泄漏地构造证据，但原文不涉及多模态与 latent 状态内容。
